summary:
Both sent-back defects are fixed, but the class they belong to is not fully closed: a `<Using>` item in a project file still reaches Start, shown by a failing repro. I also filed one gap in the excepted file and one stale corpus note.

**O-023 is fixed.** `.taad/fitness.yaml:1645-1646` now uses `[\w.:\s]*`, so `global::`, an extern-alias qualifier, spaces and line breaks around the dots are caught. The `;` is still excluded, so a match cannot run into the next directive. `RescanElevationGuardTests.MainWindowDoesNotImportOrAliasTheClass` now reads those two patterns from the entry instead of keeping its own copy.

**O-026 is fixed.**
- The Start pattern at `fitness.yaml:1643` is now `Start(?!edLine\b)`. Forwarders named `StartFor`, `StartAsync` or `StartElevated` fire, and `StartedLine` stays quiet.
- A new guard fact holds `RescanAsAdministrator.cs` to one call of the start delegate, inside Start, with Start named only once.
- Corpus rows E17-E35 each carry an `attempt1` column, recomputed from the first build's patterns.

**What I ran:**
- 214 targeted tests, all passed: the engine's two tests (`CrSl008UsingDirectiveSpellingsTests`, `RescanStartGlobalQualifiedImportTests`), the corpus and guard tests, `SettledRulesCorpus`, `ArchitectureRulesTests`, `RuleCopiesAgree`, and the offer, probe, start and endings tests.
- Fitness check: all 120 rules hold. It read 332 files, two more than before (the two new test files), so it reads the files git can see, not `obj/`.
- The `Kernel32.cs`, `RescanOfferEndingsTests.cs` and `RescanAsAdministratorStartTests.cs` hunks are comment rewrites only, from 9353a34 (the comment fixer). No behaviour changed.

**New findings:**
- **m1 (repro run, fails 3 of 3).** `Directory.Build.props:5` turns on ImplicitUsings. So `<Using Include="FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator" Static="true" />`, or its `Alias=` form, in the App project file or a root build file becomes a project-wide `global using static global::...` line. That line is written only into the generated `GlobalUsings.g.cs` under `obj`. No SL-008 entry reads those files with a pattern that fires on that item: the call-site entry reads `src/**/*.cs` only, the census skips `obj`, and Fitness does not read `obj`. A bare `Start(...)` in any App file, `OnLoaded` included, then passes every guard. The corpus note itself names "a project file" inside the class's bound, so this is a new member of a class the build claimed closed.
- **m2 (extra).** `RescanAsAdministrator.cs` is excepted from the elevation ban as a whole file. A second method there that builds its own runas `ProcessStartInfo`, without calling Start and with a name that does not begin with Start, is caught by no rule or fact. `MainWindow` could then call it from `OnLoaded`.
- **t1 (text).** Corpus row E14's note still credits "the word boundary" for letting `StartedLine` by. It is now the `(?!edLine\b)` lookahead.

The repro file was removed afterwards; git status shows only the engine's own slice files. The waived notes (O-024, O-027, O-028) and backlog item O-025 are unchanged in the code, as their decisions intend.

Second round: This round found one new problem: the forwarder check this fix added passes even when the forwarder it is meant to catch is present. The rest of the fix held up against the inputs I tried.

**The new problem (m3).** In `RescanElevationGuardTests.TheRescanFileCallsItsStartDelegateOnceInsideStartAndStartIsCalledByNoMemberOfIt`, the Start-call count uses `(?<![\w.])Start\s*\(`. That lookbehind skips any `Start(` that has a dot in front of it. It also needs a `(`, so a method group is never counted. I added two forwarders to the text of `RescanAsAdministrator.cs` in memory and ran the fact's three regexes on it:
- `RescanAsAdministrator.Start(...)`, called qualified from inside the class;
- `Go => Start`, a method group.

Both left the counts exactly as on the real file: one declaration, one delegate call, one Start. So the fact still passes with a forwarder in place. `MainWindow.xaml.cs` is excepted from the call-site rule, and its guard looks only for `RescanAsAdministrator.Start…`, so `OnLoaded` could call `RescanAsAdministrator.Rescan(root)` or `.Go(...)` and reach the prompt. That is the forwarder half of O-026, which the build reported as closed. No repro is possible without putting a forwarder into the source file itself, so this stays a note.

**What still holds.**
- **Line breaks:** the widened directive patterns stop at `;` and handle CRLF.
- **Prefixes:** an `@` verbatim prefix on the class name still matches.
- **Flags and flavour:** `(?m)(?i)` and the `(?!edLine\b)` lookahead are valid in the Fitness engine, which checks every rule and reports them all holding.
- **Reader:** `ReadRule` reads the entry the same way under CRLF and with a BOM.
- **Product code:** nothing changed in this fix apart from a comment in `Kernel32.cs`.

**Not filed again.** Some spellings are exotic and nobody writes them by accident: `RescanAsAdministrator.@Start`, Unicode escapes in the name, and a comment between a directive's tokens (the builder already flagged that last one). The lock and partial-failure prompts have nothing new to apply to here.

findings.evidence: Directory.Build.props:5 <ImplicitUsings>enable</ImplicitUsings>. The call-site entry at .taad/fitness.yaml:1640-1647 has files: src/**/*.cs. The manifest entries over src/** and Directory.Build.* ban only ApplicationManifest, Win32Manifest and Win32Resource. src/FsAnalyser.App/obj/.../FsAnalyser.App.GlobalUsings.g.cs exists, so the SDK's GenerateGlobalUsings target runs for this project.
findings.fix: Add '(?m)(?i)<Using\s+Include\s*=\s*"[^"]*\bRescanAsAdministrator\b' to an entry that reads project and build files: the two manifest entries over src/** and Directory.Build.*, or a new entry over src/** with MainWindow.xaml excepted. Add corpus rows E36 (<Using Include="FsAnalyser.App.RescanAsAdministrator" Static="true" />, fire, attempt1 quiet), E37 (the Alias="RA" form, fire) and E38 (<Using Include="System.Text.Json" />, quiet).

findings.claim:
The new fact TheRescanFileCallsItsStartDelegateOnceInsideStartAndStartIsCalledByNoMemberOfIt holds RescanAsAdministrator.cs only to calling its `start` delegate once and naming `Start(` once. The file is excepted wholesale from 'only the rescan button's file asks Windows for elevation', so a second member there can elevate without either:
- it builds its own ProcessStartInfo with UseShellExecute = true and Verb = ElevationVerb;
- it calls Process.Start directly, and its name does not begin with Start.
No rule or fact catches it. MainWindow.xaml.cs could then call that member from OnLoaded or ShowOutcome: MainWindow is excepted from the call-site entry, and the guard test looks only for StartName. The fitness because text ('A forwarder that RescanAsAdministrator.cs itself would add is held by RescanElevationGuardTests') covers only a forwarder that calls Start.
findings.evidence: RescanElevationGuardTests.cs:112-128 counts `(?<![\w.])start\s*\(` and `(?<![\w.])Start\s*\(` only. RescanAsAdministrator.cs:116-121 is the one place UseShellExecute and ElevationVerb are used today, and nothing pins that.
findings.fix: Extend the fact: in RescanAsAdministrator.cs, `UseShellExecute`, `ElevationVerb` (outside its own declaration), `new ProcessStartInfo` and `Process.Start(` (outside crefs) occur only inside Start's brace-matched body.

findings.claim: Corpus row E14's note says StartedLine is let by 'the word boundary'. Since this fix, the Start pattern is `Start(?!edLine\b)`, so a word boundary no longer separates them; the negative lookahead excludes StartedLine.

quote.text: "note": "StartedLine is not Start: the word boundary"

findings.fix: Change the note to 'StartedLine is not Start: the pattern's (?!edLine\b) lets it by, and any other Start... member fires'.

findings.claim:
The forwarder fact added for O-026 cannot see the two common forwarder shapes. Its Start-call count is `(?<![\w.])Start\s*\(`.
- The lookbehind drops any `Start(` with a dot before it. That was meant for the `Process.Start(` cref, but it also drops a qualified self-call `RescanAsAdministrator.Start(...)` inside the class.
- The `\(` means a method group `=> Start;` is never counted.
Measured by running the fact's three regexes on the file's text with each forwarder appended in memory:
- `public static string? Rescan(string root) => RescanAsAdministrator.Start(Environment.ProcessPath, root, Process.Start);` gives decl=1, delegate=1, startNamed=1, the same as the real file, so the fact passes;
- `public static Func<string?, string, Func<ProcessStartInfo, Process?>, string?> Go => Start;` gives the same counts.
The file is excepted from the call-site entry, MainWindow.xaml.cs is excepted too, and MainWindow's guard looks only for `RescanAsAdministrator\s*\.\s*Start(?!edLine\b)`. So `RescanAsAdministrator.Rescan(root)` or `.Go(...)` called from OnLoaded or ShowOutcome reaches the elevation and trips nothing. This is a member of the class O-026 was closed as.
findings.class_of: spellings that reach RescanAsAdministrator.Start without spelling RescanAsAdministrator.Start
findings.evidence: The fact is at RescanElevationGuardTests.cs:112-128. Its comment at :110-111 says 'Start is not called by another member of that file'. In the real file today, `\bStart\b` occurs only in doc comments (cref="Start", cref="Process.Start(...)", 'VolumeSpace.Start') and in the declaration.
findings.fix: Strip `//` and `///` comment text from the file before counting, then require `(?<!Process\s*\.\s*)\bStart\b` to occur exactly once, at the declaration. That counts qualified self-calls, bare calls and method groups alike. Add two corpus-style rows to the fact's own theory: the qualified forwarder and the method-group forwarder above, each expected to fail the count.
